title: How France Wrote Women Out of the Crown
dek: Of how two regents took the throne over a king's daughter and a king's grandson, and how a Frankish land code was found later to justify it.

panels.label: Valois Told It
panels.text: An ancient law of the Franks barred women from the French crown and from passing it on, and every king since Clovis had obeyed it.

panels.label: Evidence Allows
panels.text: The rule was made in 1317 and 1328 by assemblies backing the strongest claimant. The Salic code was first cited for it around 1358.

panels.label: The Entry
panels.text: Assemblies, 1317 and 1328, then a text found c. 1358.
